clue.text: Work clearin' sty out on a farm

indicators.note: on says the rearranged letters are added to the end of the farm piece

parts.note: a stud is a farm where horses are bred

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmhand has the mucky job of emptying the pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the first Sherlock Holmes novel, a work in the literary sense rather than a chore; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'on' only fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes novel is a literary work.

clue.text: Fuel a miner initially locates when working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are in motion, so the pieces before it are rearranged
initially takes only the opening letter of miner

explanation.surface: A pit worker finds something to burn while on shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when working' rearranges A, M (from 'miner initially') and LOCATES. The whole clue also paints the answer nicely, since a miner digs it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a grade of the black mineral burned in boilers to raise steam.

clue.text: Dish, hot one, after some uncooked seafood starters

indicators.note: after says hot and one follow the opening letters picked from the other words
starters points at the opening letters of the three words before it

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spicy main course follows a few raw fish appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' takes the opening letters of 'some uncooked seafood', and 'after' places H and I behind them. The surface cheekily describes the answer, which is anything but hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Japanese rice-and-raw-fish speciality is a kind of food served on a plate.

clue.text: Little weight attached to my award

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: The speaker thinks their prize is not taken very seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the American music industry's annual prize.

clue.text: Bird with a nest originally accommodating cuckoo there

indicators.note: accommodating means the a-plus-letter pair makes room for the other piece inside it
originally takes the opening letter of nest
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird finds that a cuckoo has moved into its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The cuckoo is not a bird here but a word for mad, signalling the anagram, while 'accommodating' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a moorhen or similar wading rail is one species of feathered creature.

clue.text: Threaten demon with death

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: Someone menaces a devil with being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a storm that looms is one that hangs over you menacingly.

clue.text: Poem as exercise

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
to exercise is to train

explanation.surface: Verse is treated as a workout for the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny word 'as' is not a link here: it gives QUA, the Latin word meaning 'in the capacity of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a four-line stanza is one short form of verse.

clue.text: Sexually attracted fit English teacher

parts.note: a turn is a fit, a sudden attack of illness
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Somebody fancies an athletic schoolmaster who teaches literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a description of the teacher, but it is a noun: a funny turn is a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe someone who has been aroused by another person.

clue.text: Soldiers detaining deserter without charge

indicators.note: detaining means the soldiers hold the deserter inside themselves

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: Troops hold a runaway but have not formally accused him.
explanation.walkthrough: The charge is not a criminal accusation but a price, and 'detaining' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something given for nothing costs no money.

clue.text: Fairly wide track closed by mistake

indicators.note: closed by means the track is enclosed, shut inside the mistake

parts.note: bish is old British slang for a blunder
a track is a rough road

explanation.surface: A reasonably broad path has been shut off in error.
explanation.walkthrough: The mistake is dated British schoolboy slang for a blunder; 'closed by' means enclosed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the suffix makes the adjective mean somewhat ample in breadth.

clue.text: Jumper European primate held in both hands

indicators.note: held in means the two pieces sit between the two hands

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two hands
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Someone clutches a sweater from the Continent, or perhaps a monkey, in two hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' puts E and APE between L and R. To British readers a jumper is a sweater, but here it is simply one who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are someone or something that springs into the air.

clue.text: Spades and clubs discarded in very appealing card game

indicators.note: discarded in means the two suit letters are thrown out of the word for very appealing

parts.note: scrummy is British slang for delicious or very attractive
S is the abbreviation for spades in card notation
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card notation

explanation.surface: A player throws away black cards during an enjoyable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded in' removes S and C from SCRUMMY, British slang for delicious. Discarding is itself what players do in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a pastime in which players collect sets and runs from a pack.

clue.text: In the event, half of them will enter competition fixed for later?

indicators.note: will enter means the half-word goes inside the word for competition

parts.note: a trial is a competition, as in time trial or sheepdog trial

indicators.note: half of takes the first two letters of the four-letter word them

parts.note: an event that is on is scheduled to take place

explanation.surface: As it turns out, only half the entrants will take part in a contest rearranged for a later date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the event' reads as 'as it turned out', hiding the sporting definition; 'will enter' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the swim-bike-run race is one sporting contest.

clue.text: Almost bankrupt craft shop spared collapse

indicators.note: collapse tells the three words before it to fall apart and be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A nearly insolvent handicraft store narrowly avoids going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' rearranges CRAFT SHOP SPARED. 'spared' looks like the verb of the sentence but is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone very short of money is close to insolvency.

clue.text: Weapon for one involved in attack shortly

indicators.note: involved in means the short abbreviation is wrapped up inside the trimmed word
shortly cuts the word for attack short by its last letter

parts.note: to assail is to attack
for one means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: An armament is needed by a person who will soon take part in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' is not 'for one person' but 'for example'; 'shortly' drops a final letter before 'involved in' does the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a light spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Male entering race ahead of a Greek character

indicators.note: ahead of says the race-and-male piece comes before the final letter
entering means the male pronoun goes inside the race

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man joins a marathon, starting in front of a runner from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: The race is the Tourist Trophy, the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man. The character is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the eighth letter of the Hellenic alphabet.

clue.text: Women of easy virtue acted up and conned men regularly

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for acted is written from bottom to top

parts.note: mimed means acted without words

indicators.note: regularly takes every second letter of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Loose ladies behaved badly and repeatedly swindled gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acted up' reads as 'misbehaved' but splits in two: a verb, then 'up' as the reversal signal. 'regularly' picks the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the French term names the class of kept mistresses on society's fringe.

clue.text: Single small business needing new image

parts.note: a single is one, written I
Co is the short form of company, a business

explanation.surface: A one-person firm wants to rebrand itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: it is a picture, originally a sacred painting and now also a symbol on a screen.

clue.text: British colleague's backed American students' programme

indicators.note: backed means the British-plus-colleague run is written backwards

parts.note: a colleague is an ally, and the possessive adds the S
US means American

explanation.surface: A UK co-worker has supported a course for scholars from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like 'supported' in the surface, but it turns the first two pieces round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: it is the outline of what a course of study covers.

clue.text: A pound off fabric in one part of supermarket

indicators.note: off means the pound letter is taken away from the fabric

parts.note: lisle is a fine cotton fabric used for stockings
L is the old abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Cloth is reduced by a quid in one section of the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L (the pound) from LISLE, a smooth cotton fabric. The surface reads as a price cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: shoppers walk down this passage between the shelves.

clue.text: Gave up painting dingy hotels at the front

indicators.note: at the front says the rearranged hotels come first, before the painting
dingy means dirty or messy, so the letters of hotels are disordered

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A decorator abandoned the job of doing up some shabby seafront guesthouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painting' looks like the thing given up but is a noun; 'dingy' is an unusual anagram signal, in the sense of dirtied or messed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to become discouraged is to stop trying.

clue.text: Where signing of postwar treaty was held up by newsmen on air tonight

definitions.text: Where signing of postwar treaty was

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Broadcasters going out live this evening delayed the signing of a peace accord.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1920 treaty between the Allies and Hungary after the First World War was signed at this palace at Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand palace of this name at Versailles hosted the 1920 peace agreement with Hungary.

clue.text: Theatre company set up by one-time actor

indicators.note: set up, in a down clue, means the theatre company is written upwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company with a stock of plays
one-time means former

explanation.surface: A drama troupe was founded by someone who used to tread the boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time actor' reads as a unit but splits between wordplay and definition; 'set up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are someone who appears on stage.

clue.text: Harrier in pieces, stuck between peaks

indicators.note: stuck between means the pieces are wedged in the gap between the two peaks

parts.note: a tor is a rocky peak, so two peaks give it twice
men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A jump jet lies in bits, wedged between two mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck between' puts MEN, chess pieces, between two TORs. The Harrier is neither jet nor hawk: it is one who harries.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who harries is one who persistently torments.

clue.text: Cut of meat top dog fails to finish

parts.note: top is number one, written No. 1 and read as letters

indicators.note: fails to finish means the dog loses its last letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: The alpha hound leaves some of its steak uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' is number one, written NO I. 'fails to finish' drops the last letter of SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a small round piece of lamb or other flesh sold by butchers.

clue.text: Label on child's, not women's, jackets

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means the label sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: a tab is a small label

indicators.note: not means the letter for women's is left out of the word for child's

parts.note: a ward is a child in a guardian's care, and the possessive adds the S
W is the abbreviation for women's, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: The tag is sewn into kids' coats, not ladies' ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes W (women's) from WARDS, and 'on' puts TAB above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: they are short sleeveless garments once worn over armour.

clue.text: In school, before cross-country event, there's cold squash

indicators.note: In means the cold-and-event pair goes inside the school
before says the cold letter precedes the event

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a cross-country event is a run

explanation.surface: Pupils get a chilled fruit drink ahead of the long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: To Britons squash is a fruit cordial or a racket sport; here it is the verb crush. 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean to crush or crumple something.

clue.text: Say no more about your dessert tipping over

indicators.note: tipping over, in a down clue, means the whole assembled run is turned upside down
about means the dessert goes round the word for your

parts.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the trifle you knocked onto the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The dessert is the British short form of pudding. 'about' builds the container first, then 'tipping over' turns the whole thing upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an actor who forgets their lines falls silent.

clue.text: Raised a street guide covering large Spanish city

indicators.note: covering means the upturned run wraps round the letter for large
Raised, in a down clue, means the a-plus-guide run is written upwards

parts.note: a street guide is a map
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone held aloft an A to Z showing a big town in Iberia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns A MAP into PAMA, and 'covering' wraps that round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the capital of Majorca in the Balearic Islands.

clue.text: Jack and I coming first, females second

indicators.note: coming first says the jack and I are placed ahead of the females

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
F is the abbreviation for female, so two females are FF

explanation.surface: Two boys win the race and the girls are runners-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' reads as a finishing position but is a moment of time. 'coming first' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean a very brief moment.
